Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden p95/p99 spikes on inference startup (us-west)

Karthik — investigated immediately. Findings:
- A controller heuristic that aggressively scales down 'idle' warm pools ran as part of the 15:30 maintenance. The heuristic misclassified some recent sessions as idle due to a metrics scrape delay.
- Prefix cache invalidation did run at 15:34 but was not the primary driver — the larger impact came from the eviction.

Mitigation applied (16:20 PST):
- Increased warm-pool retention for instances tagged 'edgewave' in us-west to 60m (was 10m).
- Backfilled 12 GPU-backed warm instances to restore KV cache for recently-used lanes.
- Temporarily disabled the aggressive downscale heuristic while we patch the scrape-timing check.

I attached a short incident_log.txt with controller events and the warm-pool rewarm traces. Early telemetry shows p95 dropping toward baseline; p99 still elevated for a small tail. I'll follow up with the exact traffic graphs once they've finished ingesting.

Laura Bennett
Director, Serving Platform, Redwood Inference

Subject: Incident update: us-west initialization latency wave — mitigation & next steps

Hi Maria / EdgeWave team — thank you for your patience and for the traces you provided. Short update and next steps: 

What we observed: a mis-tuned downscale heuristic executed during a maintenance window which, combined with a metrics scrape delay, evicted warm pools that should have been preserved. The eviction caused an initialization latency wave for idle sessions in us-west; p95 saw a ~10–15x spike for the first token window in affected requests.

What we did:
- Immediate mitigation: increased warm-pool retention for EdgeWave traffic and backfilled warm instances (applied 16:20 PST).
- Rollback: disabled the aggressive downscaler and rolled out a patch to avoid eviction on scrape anomalies (deployed 22:10 PST).
- Monitoring: we added a synthetic that hits short sequences every 45s to ensure warm-pool health and detect regressions.

Current status (09:30 PST 2026-11-15):
- p95 is within normal range for EdgeWave traffic; p99 tail reduced significantly but may briefly spike during noisy periods.
- No ongoing throttles or request failures observed; all traffic is healthy.

Root cause (high level): controller downscale heuristic + metrics scrape timing anomaly leading to unintended warm pool evictions. Full timeline and technical RCA will be posted to the incident page.

Next steps / action items for Redwood:
- Postmortem: file with RCA, timeline, and remediation plan (link below).
- Controls: add safety checks to scaling heuristics to consult recent request logs before evicting tagged warm pools.
- Compensation: if you had measurable business impact, we can escalate to account leadership for credits review (please indicate).

Links: status page: https://status.redwood.inference/incidents/2026-11-14-init-latency
